name: Stonecross Albion

location.about: An old iron town on the edge of Millbrook, swallowed by the city's spread but never part of it: 200,000 people, the blast furnaces gone, the canal and the brick terraces still there. The boundary runs down the middle of the Hallow Road - and so does the Midlands Derby.

colours.story: Amber and claret - the glow of the Stonecross blast furnaces at night and the colour of the iron ore. Chosen by the ironworkers who founded the club in 1880.

home.shirt: amber with claret collar and claret cuffs

rivals.why: the big city across the Hallow Road - richer, bigger, and never once a Crown of Europe winner
beaten in two Crown of Europe finals, 2000 and 2005 - Northwick have never forgiven them

history.title: The ironworks club
history.text: Founded in 1880 by men from the Stonecross furnaces. Champions in 1894 - only the sixth season of the League - and Founders' Cup winners in 1913.

history.title: Up and down
history.text: Relegated in the twenties, back up as Second Division champions in 1927 and again in 1931 after another fall; second in 1935, the same year they lost the cup final. Down after the war, champions of the Second Division again in 1951.

history.title: So close
history.text: Second in 1964 and 1976 - the year of the club's second Founders' Cup - and Charter Cup finals lost in 1962, 1973 and 1980. Relegated in the mid-eighties and promoted as runners-up in 1987; second again in 1990.

history.title: Kings of the continent
history.text: Champions in 1993. Then the greatest nights in the club's history: the Crown of Europe in 2000 and again in 2005, both finals won against Northwick, and both followed by the Intercontinental Cup. Champions again in 2007.

history.title: The crash
history.text: Three years after the title, the money had gone: relegated in 2010. They bounced straight back - Second Division champions in 2011 and Founders' Cup winners in the same spring.

history.title: Albion again
history.text: Champions in 2019, second in 2022. And the Charter Cup? Never won - five finals lost, the last in 2025 to Millbrook, of all clubs.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1894 = 1893-94).

legends.name: Henk de Vries
legends.note: Two Crowns of Europe, two Intercontinental Cups, two titles. The de Vries Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Marcus Bell
legends.note: Scored the winner in both Crown of Europe finals against Northwick.

legends.name: Ray Doolan
legends.note: From the Second Division in 1986 to the title in 1993.

records.attendance: 64,880 v Millbrook United, League, 1949 (Furnace Lane, before seating)

badge.about: The stone cross the town is named after, standing in the furnace's glow; two stars for the Crowns of Europe. Motto 'Ex Igne Fortitudo' - from the fire, strength.
badge.design: An amber shield with a claret border. In the centre a tall claret stone cross (an old market cross) with flames in claret and white rising behind it. Two small white stars above the cross. 'STONECROSS ALBION' arched above the shield in claret capitals, and a claret ribbon beneath reading 'EX IGNE FORTITUDO' in amber.

ground.name: Furnace Lane

stands.name: de Vries Stand
stands.features: the main stand, built with the Crown of Europe money: tunnel, dugouts, boxes, the two cups in the trophy room

stands.name: Furnace Bank
stands.features: the home end - one of the biggest single tiers in the country, amber seats, steep and loud

stands.name: Canal Stand
stands.features: two tiers backing onto the canal; the next to be rebuilt

stands.name: Ironworks End
stands.features: away fans in the upper tier; the last blast furnace's chimney behind it

ground.surroundings: a canal along the east side with narrowboats, red-brick terraces and an old ironworks chimney, the towers of Millbrook three miles away
ground.atmosphere: noisy and old-fashioned - the Furnace Bank is famous, and derby day against Millbrook is the loudest afternoon in the Midlands
